plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the step-by-step construction of the line graph (also called the edge graph or adjoint graph) of an undirected graph, presented in three labeled sub-panels (a, b, c). Panel a), titled ‘Original graph’, shows a 6-node undirected graph whose nodes are filled orange-colored circles labeled 1 through 6, connected by thin black undirected edges. Panel b) shows the intermediate transformation step, annotated with the instruction ‘Add new node at each original edge’: a new teal circle is placed at the position of each edge of the original graph, with the original 6 nodes still visible. Panel c), titled ‘Edge graph’, shows the resulting line graph, in which each new node is labeled by the pair of original endpoint nodes it represents (e.g., ‘2/3’, ‘1/4’, ‘4/6’, ‘1/6’, ‘4/5’, ‘2/5’, ‘1/3’), and the annotation ‘Connect new nodes if original edges shared node’ explains the rule for drawing new edges between them. All graph nodes across panels use the same teal fill color (#a0d9d3) and thin black outlines, while edges are drawn as plain black lines without arrowheads. This figure introduces the adjoint or line graph transformation, in which each edge of the original graph becomes a node in the new graph, a construct used in edge-centric graph neural network architectures.

interactionPlan.concept: The line (adjoint/edge) graph transformation: every edge of the original graph becomes a node, and two such nodes are connected whenever the original edges shared an endpoint.
elements: Three panel labels: 'a)', 'b)', 'c)' in the upper-left of each panel
Panel titles: 'Original graph' (a) and 'Edge graph' (c)
Panel a: six orange circular nodes with black outlines labeled 1,2,3,4,5,6
Panel a edges (thin black, no arrowheads): 1-3, 2-3, 2-5, 1-5, 1-4, 4-5, 1-6, 4-6
Panel b: the same six orange nodes, plus eight teal circular nodes placed at the midpoint of each original edge, labeled 2/3, 1/3, 2/5, 1/5, 1/4, 4/5, 1/6, 4/6
Panel b: original black edges now each split into two segments passing through the new teal node
Panel c: only the eight teal nodes, laid out in roughly the same relative positions, connected by black edges wherever the two original edges shared an endpoint (15 edges total)
Grey arrow between panels a and b with caption 'Add new node at each original edge'
Grey arrow between panels b and c with caption 'Connect new nodes if original edges shared node'
Color key implicit: orange = original vertices, teal (#a0d9d3) = edge-nodes
Highlight styling used by interactions: selected original edge in bold accent color, corresponding teal node ringed, generated line-graph edges drawn in the same accent color
Optional readout text showing the shared endpoint and the count of connections generated by a selected edge

interactions.label: Construction step
interactions.teaches: The transformation is two deliberate operations: first every edge is promoted to a vertex, then adjacency is inherited from shared endpoints.
Each original edge maps to exactly one node of the line graph, and its degree there equals the number of other edges touching its two endpoints.

interactions.label: Show
interactions.teaches: Comparing the two structures directly reveals that a low-degree original graph can produce a much denser line graph.

demo_steps.title: The original graph
demo_steps.narration: Six orange vertices joined by eight undirected edges. Note the hub: vertex 1 touches four of the eight edges.

demo_steps.title: Promote every edge to a node
demo_steps.narration: A teal node is dropped onto each original edge and named by its endpoints, so 1-3 becomes '1/3'. Eight edges give exactly eight new nodes.

demo_steps.title: Inherit adjacency from shared endpoints
demo_steps.narration: Two teal nodes get connected whenever their original edges met at a vertex. Every original vertex of degree d turns into a fully connected clique of d teal nodes.

demo_steps.title: Read off the edge graph
demo_steps.narration: Dropping the orange scaffolding leaves the line graph: 8 nodes and 15 edges. Click any original edge to see which teal node it became and which clique it belongs to.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Each vertex of degree d in the original graph becomes a complete clique of d nodes in the line graph — adjacency of edges replaces adjacency of vertices, which is why edge-centric GNNs can operate on this dual structure.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three horizontal panels on white. Panel a (left): six orange (#d2714d) circles with black outlines labeled 1-6, arranged as in the figure — 3 top, 2 upper-left, 1 right-of-center, 5 far left, 4 lower-left, 6 lower-right; edges 1-3, 2-3, 2-5, 1-5, 1-4, 4-5, 1-6, 4-6 as thin plain black lines. Panel b (middle): same layout with a teal (#a0d9d3) circle sitting at the midpoint of each edge, labeled with the endpoint pair (2/3, 1/3, 2/5, 1/5, 1/4, 4/5, 1/6, 4/6); black lines now run vertex-to-teal-node-to-vertex. Panel c (right): only the eight teal nodes, keeping their approximate relative positions, densely interconnected (15 edges) with the tightest cluster around 1/5, 1/4, 1/3, 1/6 because vertex 1 has degree four. Two thick grey right-pointing arrows sit below the gaps between panels with two-line captions 'Add new node at each original edge' and 'Connect new nodes if original edges shared node'. Panel letters a), b), c) in the top-left of each panel in large light text; titles 'Original graph' and 'Edge graph' centered above panels a and c. Interaction highlights should use a single warm accent (e.g. gold/amber) for the selected edge, its teal counterpart node, and the edges it generates, dimming everything else to light grey.

attempts.html:
Line-graph builder

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: All node labels inside circles (orange 1–6 and teal 2/3, 1/5, …) render at roughly 7–8 px at the inline scale because the 1630×615 viewbox is squeezed into a ~580 px-wide container, so they are noticeably harder to read than in the source where the numbers are prominent.

In panel b) the teal edge-nodes are placed at exact edge midpoints, whereas the source offsets several of them off-midpoint (e.g. 2/3 and 1/3 bulge outward, 1/5 sits well inside), giving the source a slightly rounder, less cluttered arrangement.

Panel c) node layout is only an approximation of the source arrangement (1/5, 1/4, 1/6 cluster more tightly), so a few edge crossings differ from the original drawing even though the topology (15 edges) is correct.
The figure is drawn with large empty margins above and below inside the container (aspect-ratio letterboxing), making the whole diagram read smaller than the source's tight crop.
Step 4 ('Connect shared') colours the line-graph edges by shared vertex — a colour scheme not present in the monochrome-edge source (acceptable pedagogically, but an addition).
evaluation.notes: Faithful three-panel reproduction with correct 8-edge original graph, correct 8 edge-nodes and correct 15-edge line graph, plus a genuinely useful 5-step builder, phase toggles and click-to-trace selection; the main weaknesses are small in-node label text at inline scale and midpoint-only placement of the panel-b teal nodes.
action_items: Reduce the viewbox to tightly crop the artwork (or increase in-node font sizes to ~28–32 user units) so the 1–6 and 2/3-style labels remain comfortably legible when scaled to the inline container width.
Nudge panel-b teal nodes off exact midpoints to match the source's outward bulge for 2/3, 1/3 and inward placement for 1/5, reducing overlap with the orange vertices and the 1-5/1-4 lines.
Fine-tune posC so panel c)'s edge crossings match the source layout more closely (spread 1/5, 1/4, 1/6 slightly)
Trim vertical letterboxing by setting the viewbox height closer to the drawn content so the figure fills the container like the static image.

feedback.rationale: Concept, panels, and interactions are correct; remaining issues are implementation details like viewbox cropping, font sizing, and node placement tweaks.

Line-graph builder

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The whole figure renders at roughly a third of the available canvas scale (large empty area below it), so panel titles, arrow captions and node labels appear noticeably smaller and lighter-weight than the bold, generously sized typography of the source.
Node outlines and edge strokes are thinner relative to node size than in the source, giving a lighter, less graphic look than the original's heavy black outlines.

Panel b's teal edge-nodes sit exactly on the straight segment between endpoints in most cases, whereas the source bulges several of them (2/3, 1/3, 2/5, 4/5) visibly off the straight chord, producing the characteristic rounded 'beaded' contour — the generated version is flatter.

Step 3 colour-codes the edge-graph edges by shared vertex (blue/purple/green/etc.), a palette not present in the source's all-black edges (acceptable as a teaching aid, but it changes panel c's look in that step).
evaluation.notes: Topologically faithful and conceptually correct three-panel line-graph construction (8 vertices/edges, 15 edge-graph edges, correct cliques) with a rich, working step player, phase buttons, view toggle and click-to-trace selection; main weaknesses are the small rendered scale with excess whitespace making labels and stroke weights lighter than the bold source styling.

Increase node stroke width and label font sizes relative to node radius to match the source's heavy black outlines and large numerals.
Restore the outward bulge of the teal edge-nodes in panel b (2/3, 1/3, 2/5, 4/5) so the bead chain curves as in the original rather than lying flat on the chords.
Consider making the step-3 clique colour coding optional (toggle) so the default/step-0 state and step 4 stay all-black like the source.

discrepancies: At the default inline size the SVG (viewBox 1616 wide) is compressed into roughly the left 600 px beside the control panel, so the caption text ('Add new node at each original edge', 'Connect new nodes if original edges shared node') and the node labels render very small compared with the prominent typography of the source.

In panel b the teal edge-nodes bulge outward less than in the source, so the characteristic 'bead chain' curve around the outside of the graph (2/3, 2/5, 4/5, 4/6) is flatter and the panel reads as a straighter polygon than the original.

Panel titles are placed slightly off-centre relative to their panels (e.g. 'Original graph' at x=268 over a panel spanning ~40–480), and the a)/b)/c) letters sit a bit further from the titles than in the source; cosmetic only.
Node outline/edge stroke weights are proportionally thinner than the heavy black strokes of the source, giving a slightly lighter overall look.
claude-opus-5.notes: A faithful three-panel reproduction with the correct 6-vertex/8-edge original graph, correct 8 edge-nodes and all 15 line-graph edges, plus a rich and pedagogically apt set of interactions (step player, phase buttons, view filter, clique colouring, click-to-trace); the main weaknesses are small text/label sizes at the default inline width and slightly flatter panel-b bead placement.
